# Moiré-Based Deformation Measurement Method

## Overview of the Measuring Sheet Structure

The measuring method employs a specially designed sheet composed of two distinct layer portions. The first layer portion features a first pattern of line drawings that extend in a first direction, while the second layer portion contains a second pattern of line drawings extending in a different, second direction. This deliberate difference in orientation between the two patterns is fundamental to the operation of the measurement technique.

## Generation of the Moiré Pattern

When the two layer portions are overlaid upon one another, the interaction between their respective line drawings produces a moiré pattern. This moiré effect arises from the optical interference created by the superimposition of the two differently oriented line patterns. Because the moiré pattern is highly sensitive to even minute variations in the relative positioning and spacing of the underlying lines, it serves as an effective visual indicator of changes occurring within the sheet.

## Application to the Measurement Subject

To capture deformation-related information, the sheet is disposed directly on the measurement subject. As the subject undergoes deformation, the sheet deforms in correspondence with it. This deformation alters the configuration of the line drawings within each layer portion, which in turn modifies the resulting moiré pattern. In this way, the sheet translates physical deformation of the subject into observable changes in the moiré pattern.

## Acquisition of Post-Deformation Image Data

Following deformation of the measurement subject, the method acquires post-deformation image data. This image data corresponds to an image that includes a post-deformation moiré—that is, the moiré pattern created by the overlaid, now-deformed line patterns. By recording this image, the method captures a detailed representation of the deformed state of the sheet and, by extension, of the measurement subject itself.

## Determination of the Amount of Deformation

Finally, the amount of deformation of the measurement subject is determined based on the acquired post-deformation image data. By analyzing the characteristics of the post-deformation moiré pattern, the method quantifies the extent of deformation that has taken place. This approach enables precise and reliable measurement of deformation through the interpretation of the moiré pattern captured in the image data.

# Deformation Measurement Using Moiré Patterns

## Technical Field

The present disclosure relates to a method and apparatus for measuring the deformation of a subject. More specifically, it concerns a technique that employs a specially configured sheet to visualize and quantify deformation through the exploitation of optical moiré effects.

## Background

Accurate measurement of deformation is essential across numerous fields, including structural engineering, materials testing, civil infrastructure monitoring, and manufacturing quality control. When a physical body is subjected to load, stress, temperature change, or the passage of time, it may undergo deformation that is difficult to detect with the naked eye. Detecting such subtle changes reliably and with high sensitivity presents an ongoing challenge, particularly when the deformation magnitude is small relative to the size of the subject.

## Summary of the Disclosure

The present disclosure addresses the problem of measuring the deformation of a subject by using a sheet constructed from two overlaid layers. Each of these layers contains a line-drawing pattern, and the patterns of the respective layers are oriented in different directions relative to one another. When these two layers are superimposed, the interaction between the differently oriented line patterns produces a moiré effect—an interference pattern of light and dark bands that appears as a consequence of the geometric overlap of the underlying line structures.

A significant advantage of the moiré effect is its ability to amplify small displacements. Because the resulting moiré fringes shift substantially in response to comparatively minor changes in the relative position or spacing of the two line patterns, even slight deformations of the subject become readily observable and measurable.

## Method of Operation

In practice, the sheet is applied to, attached to, or otherwise associated with the target subject whose deformation is to be measured. As the subject deforms, the relative arrangement of the two overlaid layers changes accordingly, which in turn alters the moiré pattern generated by their combination.

The method includes acquiring image data of this moiré pattern after the deformation has occurred. This post-deformation image data captures the state of the moiré fringes as modified by the deformation of the subject. By analyzing the acquired image data—for example, by evaluating the position, spacing, orientation, or phase of the moiré fringes—the method determines the amount of deformation that the subject has undergone.

## Advantages

By leveraging the amplifying characteristics of the moiré effect together with image-based analysis of the resulting fringe pattern, the disclosed approach enables effective, sensitive, and reliable deformation measurement of the target subject. The technique can detect deformation that might otherwise be difficult to observe directly, offering a practical solution for a wide range of measurement applications.

# Abstract

A method and apparatus for measuring deformation in a structure or material using a moiré-based sensing sheet is disclosed. The sensing sheet comprises a first layer and a second layer overlaid in substantially parallel relation, each layer bearing a periodic array of markings such that superposition of the two layers produces a moiré interference pattern. The first and second layers are configured to undergo relative displacement in response to deformation of an underlying substrate to which the sheet is affixed. When the substrate experiences strain, bending, elongation, or other deformation, the relative movement between the layers causes a corresponding shift, rotation, or spatial-frequency change in the moiré pattern. The method includes capturing an image of the moiré pattern before and after deformation, and analyzing changes in pattern fringe position, spacing, or orientation to quantify the magnitude and direction of the deformation. Because the moiré effect amplifies small relative displacements into readily observable pattern variations, the disclosed method enables high-sensitivity measurement of deformation without complex electronic instrumentation. The invention is applicable to structural health monitoring, material testing, and strain measurement across a range of surfaces and geometries.

# Deformation Amount Measuring Method Using Two-Layer Sheet with Crossing Line Drawings for Moiré Pattern Analysis

## TECHNICAL FIELD

The present invention relates to a method for measuring the amount of deformation in a structure or material, and more particularly to a method employing a two-layer sheet arrangement having crossing line drawings that produce moiré patterns to enable visual and quantitative analysis of displacement and deformation.

## BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION

Conventional deformation measurement techniques often rely on strain gauges, extensometers, or optical interferometry systems that require complex instrumentation, precise calibration, and substantial equipment cost. Strain gauges provide only localized point measurements and require electrical connections, while interferometric methods demand controlled laboratory conditions and are sensitive to environmental vibration.

There exists a need for a simple, low-cost, and visually intuitive method for detecting and quantifying deformation over an area of interest, particularly for structural health monitoring applications where continuous or periodic inspection is desirable.

## SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

The present invention provides a deformation amount measuring method utilizing a two-layer sheet assembly. Each layer bears a line drawing pattern comprising a plurality of substantially parallel lines. When the two layers are superimposed with their respective line patterns crossing at a predetermined angle, an optical interference effect known as a moiré pattern is generated. Relative displacement between the two layers, caused by deformation of an underlying substrate, produces a corresponding shift, rotation, or spacing change in the moiré pattern that is magnified relative to the actual displacement.

The magnification effect inherent in the moiré phenomenon enables detection of small deformations that would otherwise be difficult to observe, thereby permitting accurate quantitative measurement of the deformation amount.

## BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF THE DRAWINGS

- **FIG. 1** is a perspective view of the two-layer sheet assembly.
- **FIG. 2** is a plan view showing the crossing line drawings of the first and second layers.
- **FIG. 3** illustrates the moiré pattern generated in an undeformed state.
- **FIG. 4** illustrates the shifted moiré pattern following deformation.
- **FIG. 5** is a flowchart of the measurement method.

## DETAILED DESCRIPTION

### Structure of the Two-Layer Sheet

The measuring apparatus comprises a **first sheet layer (10)** and a **second sheet layer (20)**, each formed of a substantially transparent or translucent flexible material such as a polymer film (e.g., polyethylene terephthalate).

The **first sheet layer (10)** bears a first line drawing (11) comprising a plurality of first parallel lines arranged at a first pitch P₁. The **second sheet layer (20)** bears a second line drawing (21) comprising a plurality of second parallel lines arranged at a second pitch P₂.

The two layers are superimposed such that the first line drawing (11) and the second line drawing (21) cross at a predetermined crossing angle θ, thereby forming a **crossing line configuration** that generates an observable **moiré pattern (30)**.

### Attachment and Coupling

The first sheet layer (10) is affixed to a first region of an object under measurement, and the second sheet layer (20) is affixed to a second region of the object, the first and second regions being spaced apart such that relative deformation of the object induces relative displacement between the two layers. Alternatively, one layer may serve as a fixed reference layer while the other is coupled to a moving portion of the object.

### Generation of the Moiré Pattern

When the first pitch P₁ and second pitch P₂ are equal or nearly equal and the crossing angle θ is small, the resulting moiré pattern exhibits a pitch P_m substantially larger than the individual line pitches, according to the relationship:

**P_m ≈ P / (2 sin(θ/2))**

where P is the common line pitch. This relationship demonstrates the inherent magnification: a small change in relative position or angle between the layers produces a proportionally larger, and thus readily observable, change in the moiré pattern.

### Measurement Principle

Upon deformation of the object, the second sheet layer (20) displaces relative to the first sheet layer (10) by a displacement amount δ. This relative displacement causes the moiré pattern (30) to shift by a magnified distance D, where the magnification factor M is given by:

**M = D / δ = P_m / P**

By measuring the shift D of the moiré pattern, the actual deformation amount δ is calculated as:

**δ = D / M**

For deformation involving relative rotation, a corresponding rotation or change in orientation of the moiré fringes is observed and correlated to the angular deformation.

### Method Steps

The deformation amount measuring method comprises the following steps:

1. **Providing** a two-layer sheet assembly having a first sheet layer bearing a first line drawing and a second sheet layer bearing a second line drawing.

2. **Superimposing** the first and second sheet layers such that the first and second line drawings cross at a predetermined angle to generate a moiré pattern.

3. **Attaching** the two-layer sheet assembly to an object under measurement such that deformation of the object produces relative displacement between the layers.

4. **Acquiring** an initial reference image of the moiré pattern in an undeformed state.

5. **Acquiring** a subsequent image of the moiré pattern after deformation has occurred.

6. **Detecting** a shift, rotation, or spacing change of the moiré pattern between the reference image and the subsequent image.

7. **Calculating** the deformation amount by dividing the measured moiré pattern displacement by the predetermined magnification factor.

### Image Acquisition and Analysis

In one embodiment, the moiré pattern is captured by an imaging device such as a digital camera or smartphone camera. An image processing unit analyzes the acquired images by identifying the positions of moiré fringe centers or by performing spatial frequency analysis (e.g., Fourier transform) to determine the fringe displacement with sub-pixel accuracy.

The image processing unit computes the deformation amount based on the detected fringe displacement and the known magnification factor, and outputs the result to a display or storage device.

### Alternative Embodiments

In an alternative embodiment, the line drawings comprise curved, radial, or grid-patterned lines rather than straight parallel lines, enabling the detection of two-dimensional deformation fields, shear deformation, or rotational deformation.

In a further embodiment, the line drawings are printed in contrasting colors to enhance the visibility of the moiré pattern under varying lighting conditions.

In yet another embodiment, one or both line drawings are formed as a chirped grating having a spatially varying pitch, providing position-dependent sensitivity across the measurement area.

## CLAIMS

**1.** A deformation amount measuring method comprising:
providing a first sheet layer bearing a first line drawing and a second sheet layer bearing a second line drawing;
superimposing the first and second sheet layers such that the first and second line drawings cross at a predetermined angle to generate a moiré pattern;
detecting a change in the moiré pattern resulting from relative displacement between the first and second sheet layers caused by deformation of an object; and
calculating a deformation amount based on the detected change in the moiré pattern and a predetermined magnification factor.

**2.** The method of claim 1, wherein the first line drawing comprises first parallel lines at a first pitch and the second line drawing comprises second parallel lines at a second pitch.

**3.** The method of claim 1, wherein detecting the change comprises acquiring a reference image and a subsequent image of the moiré pattern and determining a displacement of moiré fringes therebetween.

**4.** The method of claim 1, wherein the magnification factor is a ratio of a moiré pattern pitch to a line drawing pitch.

**5.** The method of claim 1, wherein the change in the moiré pattern comprises at least one of a shift, a rotation, and a spacing change of moiré fringes.

## ABSTRACT

A deformation amount measuring method employs a two-layer sheet assembly in which each layer bears a line drawing of substantially parallel lines. The layers are superimposed with their line drawings crossing at a predetermined angle, generating a moiré pattern. Deformation of an object to which the layers are attached produces relative displacement between the layers, causing a magnified shift or change in the moiré pattern. The deformation amount is calculated from the detected moiré pattern change and a known magnification factor, providing a simple, low-cost, and visually intuitive measurement technique.

# Method for Measuring Deformation of an Object Using a Multi-Layer Patterned Sheet

## FIELD OF THE INVENTION

The present invention relates to a method and apparatus for measuring deformation of an object, and more particularly to a deformation measurement sheet comprising a plurality of superimposed layers bearing line patterns oriented in differing directions.

## SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

In accordance with one embodiment of the present invention, there is provided a method for measuring deformation of an object, said method comprising the steps enumerated below.

## DETAILED DESCRIPTION

**Providing the Measurement Sheet**

A measurement sheet is provided, said sheet comprising a first layer and a second layer disposed in superimposed relation to one another. The first layer bears a first line pattern comprising a first plurality of substantially parallel lines extending in a first direction. The second layer bears a second line pattern comprising a second plurality of substantially parallel lines extending in a second direction, wherein said second direction is angularly offset from said first direction by a predetermined angle.

In one preferred embodiment, said predetermined angle is substantially ninety degrees (90°), whereby said first line pattern and said second line pattern are disposed in substantially orthogonal relation. In an alternative embodiment, said predetermined angle is selected from a range of greater than zero degrees (0°) and less than one hundred eighty degrees (180°).

**Affixing the Sheet to the Object**

The measurement sheet is affixed to a surface of said object such that said measurement sheet undergoes deformation substantially corresponding to deformation of said surface of said object. The affixing step may comprise adhering said sheet to said surface by means of an adhesive layer, whereby strain experienced by said object is transmitted to said measurement sheet.

**Establishing a Reference Condition**

A first optical characteristic is observed and recorded corresponding to an undeformed reference state of said measurement sheet, wherein superimposition of said first line pattern and said second line pattern produces a first interference pattern, said first interference pattern comprising a moiré fringe pattern arising from optical interaction between said first plurality of lines and said second plurality of lines.

**Observing the Deformed Condition**

Upon application of a load to said object, or upon deformation of said object by any cause, a second optical characteristic is observed and recorded, wherein relative displacement between said first line pattern and said second line pattern produces a second interference pattern differing from said first interference pattern.

**Determining Deformation**

The deformation of said object is determined by comparing said second interference pattern with said first interference pattern, wherein a change in at least one of spacing, orientation, and position of moiré fringes between said first interference pattern and said second interference pattern is correlated to a magnitude and direction of deformation of said object.

By virtue of the differing directions of said first and second line patterns, deformation components along a plurality of axes may be resolved, whereby both the magnitude and directional character of said deformation are ascertained.

## CLAIMS (Illustrative)

1. A method for measuring deformation of an object, comprising:
   - providing a sheet having a first layer bearing a first line pattern extending in a first direction and a second layer bearing a second line pattern extending in a second direction angularly offset from said first direction;
   - affixing said sheet to said object;
   - observing a first interference pattern corresponding to an undeformed state;
   - observing a second interference pattern corresponding to a deformed state; and
   - determining deformation of said object based upon a difference between said first and second interference patterns.

2. The method of claim 1, wherein said first direction and said second direction are substantially orthogonal.

---

*Note: This is a technical illustration of patent drafting style and is not intended as legal advice or as a filing-ready patent document.*
